meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hope, to rely on', paired with 'понадеяться'.

examples.trans: I hope so. Go on, act quickly!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.

meanings.en: to be liked, to make a good impression

Don't be afraid, you'll like it.

meanings.note: polite, or to several people; the first в is silent

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.
Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'almost, nearly' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Наш с вами город очень старый. Почти четыре века здесь были набеги.
examples.trans: Our town is very old. For almost four centuries there were raids here.

meanings.note: at the start of a question

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: в следующий раз = next time; следующий! = next, please!

examples.text: А ты в следующий раз на мои деньги не рассчитывай. И всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Well, next time don't count on my money. And everything will be fine.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.

meanings.note: + infinitive: Пора идти = Time to go

examples.trans: It's time for us to go.

ехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to drive, to ride

meanings.en: to go, to drive, to ride

examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ратно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Вот это дело! Потом обратно бесплатно отвезу.
examples.trans: Now we're talking! Afterwards I'll drive you back for free.
